evidence: Hays — UT Plant Resources Center Flora of Purola Preserve, N. Hays County lists Oenothera triloba among plants occurring naturally and not introduced.
Travis — UT Plant Resources Center Travis County herbarium index includes Oenothera triloba.
Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center Vascular Plants of Williamson County provides a detailed county treatment of Oenothera triloba.
target_zone_range.guardrail: No county occurrence inferred from statewide native status; named counties are supported by explicit local/herbarium/project occurrence evidence.

morphology.look_here_first: This one should jump out from ground level: a flat, essentially stemless rosette produces a large yellow four-petaled flower on an extraordinarily long, sharply 4-angled floral tube.
diagnostic_traits: acaulous/essentially stemless and usually under 10 cm tall
only basal irregularly pinnately lobed leaves
large radial yellow flower about 50–55 mm across
very long square 4-angled floral tube up to about 97 mm
4 stamens in the Williamson County treatment

confusers.separator: Both have large primrose-type flowers, but O. triloba is a flat stemless rosette with yellow flowers and an extremely long square tube; O. speciosa is leafy-stemmed, spreading/rhizomatous, and usually pink/white.

Both can have large yellow flowers and long tubes, but O. triloba is a tiny flat rosette with strongly lobed basal leaves; O. macrocarpa forms a larger leafy plant and develops a very large winged capsule.

diagnostic_roles: whole flower plus full long tube
